    Parsley 0.1.0-SNAPSHOT API

    Parsley is a Java library for causal consistency over Kafka. It ensures that every consumer processes messages in the correct causal order, even when records originate from multiple topics and partitions, by encoding each message's causal dependencies onto it and buffering records until those dependencies have been observed.

    The entire public surface lives in a single package, io.parsley, and consists of interfaces and value types; every implementation is package-private and obtained through a builder factory (CausalProducers, CausalConsumers, CausalProcessors).

    Core concepts

    Causal frontier
    The highest offset observed on each topic-partition, keyed by topic UUID so that topic deletion and recreation produce a distinct identity even when the name is reused. Carried as CausalFrontier; combine two frontiers with merge.
    Causal dependencies
    The minimum frontier a downstream consumer must have observed before a record may be delivered — the upstream producer's snapshot of what it had seen when it sent the record. Carried as CausalDependencies in a parsley-vector-clock header. A record is causally ready when isSatisfiedBy returns true against the consumer's current frontier.
    Causal buffer
    Records whose dependencies are not yet satisfied are held in a changelog-backed buffer and released as soon as the frontier catches up. A CausalBufferLimit bounds how long or how large the buffer may grow; when it fires, a configurable CausalBufferPolicy decides whether to forward the record anyway (forwardUnsafe), drop it (drop), or route it to a dead-letter sink (deadLetter).

    Entry points

    TypePurpose
    CausalProducerStamps the current causal dependencies onto every record it sends; built via CausalProducers.
    CausalConsumerA poll()-based consumer that delivers records in causal order; built via CausalConsumers.
    CausalProcessorSupplierWraps a user Kafka Streams Processor so its state access and forwards run behind the causal guarantee; built via CausalProcessors.

    Typical usage

    
// Consume with causal ordering
CausalConsumer<String, Order> consumer = CausalConsumers.<String, Order>builder(
    List.of("prices", "orders"),
    CausalBufferPolicy.forwardUnsafe(CausalBufferLimit.ofDuration(Duration.ofSeconds(30))),
    consumerConfig,
    streamsConfig).build();
ConsumerRecords<String, Order> records = consumer.poll(Duration.ofMillis(100));
records.forEach(record -> process(record));

// Produce, propagating the consumer's causal position
CausalProducer<String, Event> producer = CausalProducers.<String, Event>builder(producerConfig).build();
producer.send(new ProducerRecord<>("events", key, event), consumer.frontier().toDependencies());
